subject.title: v2026.6.x system prompt bloat causes instruction following degradation on smaller models

question: Should OpenClaw treat this smaller-model degradation as a core prompt-priority/scoping problem, and which permanent policy should own skill content, platform guidance, and small-model defaults?
rationale: The source surfaces are clear, but the durable fix can change public config/default behavior, skill prompt semantics, and session context priority; that product/API choice should not be made by cleanup automation.

options.title: Design core prompt-priority policy
options.body: Specify precedence among user instructions, AGENTS/SOUL context, activated SKILL.md content, and platform rules, then implement the smallest model-aware scoping changes needed to enforce it.

options.title: Fold budget-only work into existing trackers
options.body: Route bootstrap/tool-size mitigation to the tiered bootstrap and context compactor issues while keeping this issue for MiMo priority reproduction only.

options.title: Treat as model limitation
options.body: Document lean-mode and model-selection guidance as the supported path and close only if maintainers decide OpenClaw should not compensate for weaker instruction-priority models.

recommendation.title: Design core prompt-priority policy
recommendation.body: Specify precedence among user instructions, AGENTS/SOUL context, activated SKILL.md content, and platform rules, then implement the smallest model-aware scoping changes needed to enforce it.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal spans the skill prompt rules, system-prompt refactors, and prior maintainer-side prompt/context product decisions.
